commits.summary: Example 287's preservation reaches the checker and stops at java.util.logging's WARNING, not at bcrypt (verification pending)
commits.body:
The preservation stream's step 1. Example 287's driver (proofs/prove.py) gains an equivalence branch in the shape of example 289's: jvmcontract equivalence of PasswordMatchAdapter#matches, the adapter compiled against each release, 6.3.7 on its own pinned JARs (--before-classpath), the claim's nullable parameters, and the task's allowed change as --unchanged-unless, at the claim's bound of 80. It also gains 289's three properties: it writes evidence.json (accept.record), it builds the mutant by the replay route's recipe and ends the run when the JAR is not the one the mutant replay's receipt records (checked by hand: the rebuilt JAR is the replay's, sha256 1d099295...), and a run with --max-array-length or --unwind is marked a trial.

Where it stops now: a capped probe (13 s) got past both refusals recorded on 2026-11-16 (the nullable String, VF-028, and the String expression in the allowed change: a nullable String now makes the check a property of the pair, lib/src/pairing.rs) and stopped at 'outside the fragment: reads static field java.util.logging.Level.WARNING'. For a null, empty or non-bcrypt stored hash, BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches logs a warning through spring-jcl's JavaUtilLog, and the checker models java.util.logging only below INFO. So the brief's prediction that the first failure is the cryptography is out of date; the claim's domain includes those stored hashes, so the path is to be lifted, not excluded. Job 20261117-130445-example-287-preservation-through-the-ada records the stop at the frozen bound; the example's notes and the brief's Progress say so.

commits.summary: The run-streams tests no longer inherit a real run's watcher, so run inside a stream they cannot ask it questions
commits.body: test_brief_run.py's fixture now drops RUN_STREAMS_*, FEATURE_LOOP_* and LOOP_CONDUCTOR from the environment. A stream of the domain-advances run ran the test of a run 'without a watcher', which built its env from os.environ: inside the stream's loop that carries RUN_STREAMS_WATCHER, so the test's made-up run-streams.sh put two merge questions (streams a and b of made-up) to the real watcher, which answered them leave (run-streams-domain-advances D001, D002). Verified: the 39 tests pass with a decoy RUN_STREAMS_WATCHER and LOOP_CONDUCTOR set, and nothing is written to the decoy.

commits.summary: Every example's proof driver records identities, ends the run on a mutant that is not the replay's, and marks a trial
commits.body:
The evidence stream's step 2. examples/tools/beside_route.py holds what the five drivers (examples 286 to 290) did each in their own copy: the pinned JARs, the constructed mutant, the record (accept.record's evidence.json) and the verdict. Each driver keeps its own entry, lemmas, models, observed initializers and verifier arguments. What 289's driver alone did, all five now do: the record of the claim, the bound, each JAR, the adapter, the verifier's binary and the driver; a mutant whose JAR is not the one the newest mutant replay's receipt records ends the run; --max-array-length or --unwind (now on every driver) marks the run a trial.

Finding: 286's, 287's and 288's drivers built their mutant by another recipe than the route's (a fixed --release, no -g or -parameters, every entry recompressed), so their JAR was not the bytes the mutant replay ran, which is why acceptance could not tie their mutant-security answers to the replay. The shared module uses the route's published-mutant recipe; run offline on the pinned JARs it gives each of the five examples exactly the JAR its replay ran (286 48323d21, 287 1d099295, 288 5c72df16, 289 a3a3dbff, 290 4ee35d0b).

commits.summary: Countermodels of the pair of versions: five false proofs of agreement, reproduced and handed to the preservation stream
commits.body: The challenge stream's item 1. lib/tests/fixtures/pairing-countermodels holds two versions of five methods that differ when each runs alone on a JVM and that RegressionPair.agree (lib/src/pairing.rs) proves agreeing: the previous version sets the default locale the new one lowers under; a library static shared without --before-classpath; two unrelated RuntimeExceptions, and IllegalArgumentException against a subclass, compared by category; a scope that is false everywhere but sets the default locale before both calls. All five were Verified on the checker at lupovnmv. The order of the calls is observable: with the versions' roles swapped, and with --before-classpath, the shared-static case is a violation.

commits.summary: The pair of versions compares exceptions by class and starts each version as if it ran alone (verification pending)
commits.body: The challenge stream's five countermodels of the pair (lib/tests/fixtures/pairing-countermodels: a default locale the previous version sets, a library static shared without --before-classpath, two unrelated RuntimeExceptions, an IllegalArgumentException against its subclass, a scope that sets the default locale) were each proved to agree, though the versions differ when each runs alone. RegressionPair (lib/src/pairing.rs) now compares exceptions by class, through getClass().getName() with a copy's 'before.' prefix taken off, and calls fresh() before the scope and before each version. At fresh() the checker (bmc/mod.rs) and the interpreter clear the path's static fields and class initialization, which hold the default locale too, so no version starts in what an earlier one left; on a JVM fresh() sets the default locale back. The checker models getClass() of a Throwable the run made (bmc/runtime.rs), as its handlers already take it for that class. The README's checker-side test is added to lib/tests/pairing_countermodels.rs: it failed on all five before and passes now, each of the seven runs a violation confirmed by replay. Limit, stated in pairing.rs and lib/README.md: on a JVM a library's statics stay shared without --before-classpath, so a witness only they show is dropped there as no reproduction, never proved.

commits.summary: The checker models a line logged at WARNING as spring-jcl logs it, so example 287's preservation reaches both sides' bcrypt
commits.body:
java.util.logging at INFO, WARNING and SEVERE is now modelled under the JDK's default configuration (lib/src/bmc/runtime.rs). isLoggable is true there. A LogRecord's constructor of a level and a message (NullPointerException for a null level) and its setters do nothing a check observes. A Logger's resource bundle and bundle name are null. Logger.log(record) returns normally under a second stated assumption: the record goes only to the root's default ConsoleHandler, and no logger has a filter, handler or bundle. The handler formats the record by calling its getters, which a subclass may override. So log is modelled only for a record whose class below LogRecord writes nothing but its own fields and calls nothing but its own methods, LogRecord's, String's, StackTraceElement's and a Throwable's constructors and getters. A bytecode scan checks this, and spring-jcl's LocationResolvingLogRecord passes. A logging call the model does not take is now the gap it is to a checker without the model; before, an isLoggable the model declined was counted exact. String.valueOf(Object) of a String or null is modelled before the static classification, so the gap scan still names it for other objects.

Countermodels came first, in lib/tests/fixtures/claims/claims/Logged.java. On a JVM each returns false or throws where a model that took logging for granted would say true: a record that counts its formatting, a level, a filter and a handler set on a logger, and valueOf of an object whose toString counts. All five now stop the proof. With the confinement scan disabled, the counting record was falsely verified. The claims test a_line_logged_at_warning_returns_normally_and_what_would_make_logging_observable_stops_the_proof also proves the warned path, the null cases and loud. P.loud moved there, since INFO is now modelled. lib/README.md and 287's notes say what changed.

Probes on example 287's preservation: a trial at bound 8 verifies. At the claim's bound of 80, with a 200 s timeout, the pair reaches both sides' bcrypt and ends on a spurious counterexample past the invariants of BCrypt.crypt_raw and ekskey; a JVM run shows it is no counterexample. This is the relational failure the stream's brief predicts, and step 2 starts from it. Verified with test_costs.py run --changed (26 of 26), the lint, and validate_example.py 287.
